samples.summary: PDF presence publish is not gated on `readOnly`, so a viewer share link still makes a local `doc.update` — the exact rw-PushPull denial the diff removes from `initialRoot` in the same file
samples.evidence: `PdfCollabStateProvider.onActivePageChange` does `doc.update((_r, p) => p.set({ activePage: pageIndex }))` unconditionally (pdf-collab.tsx:124-128); it is wired to page scroll for every mount, including `SharedPdfLayout`'s `readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'` (shared-document.tsx:699-712). The diff's own reasoning at pdf-collab.tsx:191-202 is that any local change is carried by the next `PushPull` with verb `rw`, which the webhook refuses for a viewer — and this PR makes enforcement the DEFAULT. The notes half of the same PR neuters `setLocalSelection` for precisely this reason (`packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts`: "publishing a caret is a `doc.update` like any other"). So a viewer scrolling a shared PDF gets its sync denied while the seeding path next to it was fixed. Same class, unchecked, in slides (`packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:2751`) and board (`packages/frontend/src/app/board/yorkie-board-store.ts:567`), neither of which has a read-only store wrapper the way docs and now notes do.

samples.summary: The docs package's read-only store — the twin this PR explicitly corrects for notes — still documents the webhook as shipping in shadow mode by default
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:39-42 states the server-side check "ships in shadow mode by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`), so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary". The new `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts` explicitly calls that claim wrong and rewrites it; the docs sibling and `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4413` ("shadow mode unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`, so in a stock…") were left describing the pre-change default.

samples.summary: Design docs outside the diff still describe shadow-as-default, and sharing.md builds a whole argument on it ("client-side `readOnly` is the write boundary")
samples.evidence: docs/design/sharing.md:208-219 — "This is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment, which puts the controller in shadow mode" — and 233-235 repeats "with the flag at its default the client-side checks are what stands there". Both are now inverted by `isYorkieAuthEnforced`. Same stale statement in docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:301, docs/design/template-gallery.md:668 and docs/design/revision-history.md:504. Nested design docs are not content- or link-checked by any lane, so nothing else will flag these.

samples.summary: A comment added by this diff states the auth webhook "ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default", contradicting the default the same diff establishes
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts (new block around the `EditorState.readOnly`/`changeFilter` extensions): "since the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default and so may not refuse the write either" — while `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts` added in the same change makes enforcing the default, and the notes read-only store note next door says the opposite.

samples.summary: `shareTokenImageUploader` is handed to `NotesView` raw, but `UploadImage`'s contract is resolve-`null`-after-reporting; a failed share-link image upload is now silent
samples.evidence: `shareTokenImageUploader` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.ts:40-49) rejects on failure. `UploadImage` is `(file) => Promise<string | null>` where `null` means "failed and already reported to the user" (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:46-51); the workspace route wraps its uploader to toast and return null (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:203-215). The notes engine swallows a rejection with `console.error` only (packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:179-190), so an editor-role share-link visitor whose upload fails sees the placeholder vanish with no message. Fix belongs on the new layout.

samples.summary: Neutering `setLocalSelection` silently removes a viewer's remote caret for every peer, a behaviour other clients' UI consumed
samples.evidence: `readOnlyNoteStore` routes `setLocalSelection` to the shared no-op, and `packages/notes/src/view/remote-selection.ts:170-172` is the only publisher — so on a viewer mount peers (`getPeerSelections()` in remote-selection.ts:181) never see that visitor's caret again. Deliberate per the comment, but it is a user-visible change to collaborators outside the diff and nothing records it in docs/design/notes/notes.md's presence section.

finding.summary: PDF presence publish is not gated on `readOnly`, so a viewer share link still makes a local `doc.update` — the exact rw-PushPull denial the diff removes from `initialRoot` in the same file
finding.evidence: `PdfCollabStateProvider.onActivePageChange` does `doc.update((_r, p) => p.set({ activePage: pageIndex }))` unconditionally (pdf-collab.tsx:124-128); it is wired to page scroll for every mount, including `SharedPdfLayout`'s `readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'` (shared-document.tsx:699-712). The diff's own reasoning at pdf-collab.tsx:191-202 is that any local change is carried by the next `PushPull` with verb `rw`, which the webhook refuses for a viewer — and this PR makes enforcement the DEFAULT. The notes half of the same PR neuters `setLocalSelection` for precisely this reason (`packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts`: "publishing a caret is a `doc.update` like any other"). So a viewer scrolling a shared PDF gets its sync denied while the seeding path next to it was fixed. Same class, unchecked, in slides (`packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:2751`) and board (`packages/frontend/src/app/board/yorkie-board-store.ts:567`), neither of which has a read-only store wrapper the way docs and now notes do.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described and is reachable for a share-link viewer. pdf-collab.tsx:124-128 performs an unconditional `doc.update((_r, p) => p.set({ activePage: pageIndex }))` with no `readOnly` check, despite `readOnly` being available in that component (pdf-collab.tsx:92, 136). The path is live for viewers: shared-document.tsx:699 sets `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` and passes it into `PdfCollabProvider` (707-712), which renders `PdfCollabBody` (736) wiring `onActivePageChange` into `PdfViewer` (pdf-collab.tsx:310), which hands it to `PdfPageView.onActive` (pdf-viewer.tsx:183), fired from an IntersectionObserver on every page entering view (pdf-viewer.tsx:376-386) — i.e. on mount and on every scroll. The guard it bypasses is in the same file (initialRoot={readOnly ? {} : initialPdfRoot()}, pdf-collab.tsx:202) whose own rationale (191-201) says any local change rides the next PushPull as `rw`, and the backend confirms `rw` PushPull is denied for a share viewer (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:284-286, 322) with enforcement on by default (108-143). The notes half of the same effort deliberately neuters the analogous presence write (packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:137-143), showing the class is recognised; slides has the same unguarded pattern at yorkie-slides-store.ts:2751. No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable, and it is in the blast-radius lane (guard applied at one entry point, adjacent entry point reaches the same local mutation). The only residual uncertainty — whether a presence-only change sets pack.HasChanges() server-side — is explicitly logged as unverified in the repo's own notes (docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-lessons.md:80-85), which keeps the finding rather than refuting it.
